Chỉ tạo phần section hero ( dùng @Gemini_Generated_Image_5q0sdy5q0sdy5q0s.png )
Design and build a premium, full-screen hero section for a high-end Vietnamese education center. The hero must feel refined, authentic, warm, trustworthy, and human. The design should communicate one simple idea: children are given an environment where they can learn, try things themselves, explore, and become more confident, while teachers guide and support them.

The hero must NOT feel like a generic school website, kindergarten website, stock-photo advertisement, or AI-generated landing page.

1. OVERALL VISUAL DIRECTION

Design language:

Premium education × authentic human interaction × real children's work × restrained typography × minimal motion.

The visual identity should combine:

warm white
deep burgundy
subtle pastel pink
natural photographic colors
refined contemporary furniture
clean architectural lines
generous whitespace
soft, understated details

The center should feel high-end and thoughtfully designed, but never like a luxury showroom.

It should still feel like a real place where children genuinely learn and create.

Avoid excessive decoration, childish visual clichés, cartoon elements, bright rainbow colors, or overly playful UI.

2. HERO IMAGE

Use a full-screen 16:9 authentic documentary photograph as the dominant visual.

The scene takes place inside a real, premium Vietnamese educational learning center during an ordinary class.

A Vietnamese teacher is naturally sitting or leaning down at the child's eye level, gently guiding one young student who is actively drawing, writing, or working on a creative learning activity.

The teacher supports the child without taking over the activity.

The child remains the protagonist:

teacher guides → child explores → child practices.

The interaction must feel spontaneous and genuinely observed.

Neither the teacher nor the child looks at the camera.

No posing.

No staged smiles.

No advertising-style interaction.

The teacher should look like they are actually teaching, not demonstrating a scene for a photographer.

A second child may appear subtly in the background, naturally engaged in their own activity, but the main visual relationship must remain between the teacher and primary child.

3. PREMIUM CLASSROOM ENVIRONMENT

The classroom should clearly feel more refined than a conventional school classroom.

Use:

warm-white walls
high-quality contemporary materials
clean architectural lines
minimalist student desks
matte off-white desk surfaces
rounded desk edges
slim white or very light champagne-metal frames
modern ergonomic light-colored chairs
refined lighting
subtle burgundy and pastel-pink accents

Absolutely no wooden desks.

No wood grain.

No rustic furniture.

No colorful plastic school furniture.

No cheap-looking classroom equipment.

No childish rainbow-colored furniture.

The furniture should communicate quality through:

material + proportion + simplicity + craftsmanship, not excessive luxury.

The environment should feel premium but genuinely used.

Include subtle realistic classroom details:

papers
pencils
drawing materials
books
art supplies
small natural signs of classroom use

Do not make the environment unnaturally clean or perfectly arranged.

4. CHILDREN'S ARTWORK WALL

Behind the students, include a dedicated wall area displaying real-looking artwork created by children who attend the center.

The artwork should:

look genuinely child-made
be slightly imperfect
have different styles and levels of ability
use crayons, colored pencils, watercolor, simple mixed media
contain natural variations in composition and technique
be displayed neatly but realistically

The artwork should feel like an actual education center proudly displaying student work.

It should subtly communicate:

“Children here actually create, practice and express themselves.”

The artwork is secondary environmental proof, not the hero subject.

Do not make the drawings professionally illustrated.

Do not make every drawing visually perfect.

Do not make the artwork look digitally generated.

5. IMAGE COMPOSITION

The image must be specifically composed for a full-screen website hero.

Place the teacher and children primarily in the RIGHT 55–60% of the frame.

Reserve approximately LEFT 40–45% as genuine negative space for typography.

The left side should contain:

a warm-white classroom wall
subtle architectural details
low visual complexity
soft natural light
enough tonal contrast for typography

Do NOT place on the left side:

faces
hands
important objects
strong visual patterns
prominent children's artwork
busy furniture

The negative space must feel like a natural part of the classroom, not an artificially erased area.

Do not divide the image into a literal “text panel” and “photo panel”.

The photograph should visually continue across the entire screen.

If necessary, use an extremely subtle soft gradient toward the left side to improve text readability.

Do not use a large white text box.

6. HEADER / NAVIGATION

Overlay a lightweight navigation directly on top of the Hero.

Structure:

LEFT

Logo

CENTER/RIGHT

Lớp học
Môi trường
Về chúng tôi

FAR RIGHT

[ Tìm lớp cho bé → ]

Do not use:

Trang chủ / Dịch vụ / Gallery / Tin tức / Liên hệ

The navigation should feel specific to the parent journey.

Header typography

Use Hind Siliguri.

Navigation:

15px
weight 500
line-height 1
no uppercase
no excessive letter spacing

CTA:

Hind Siliguri
15–16px
weight 600
Header layout

Desktop:

horizontal padding: 48–64px
top padding: 28–32px
logo width: approximately 110–125px
navigation gap: approximately 32px
CTA separated from navigation by approximately 32–40px

The header must remain visually quiet.

Do not allow the header to compete with the teacher, child, or headline.

7. NAVIGATION HOVER

Navigation items should have a very subtle interaction.

On hover:

a thin 2px underline appears from left to right
duration: approximately 220ms
ease-out

Do not change font weight on hover.

Do not use large animated backgrounds.

Do not use icons beside every navigation item.

8. SCROLL HEADER STATE

Initially, the header is transparent over the Hero.

After approximately 60px of scrolling, transition it into a refined floating header:

warm-white / white translucent background
approximately 92% opacity
backdrop blur around 10–14px
dark/burgundy typography
extremely subtle shadow
approximately 72px height

Transition duration:

250–350ms ease-out.

Do not make the header suddenly slide down from the top.

It should feel like the same header simply changing state.

9. HERO TYPOGRAPHY

Keep the copy extremely short.

The image carries most of the story.

Headline

“Để con được học, thử và tự tin hơn.”

Use a refined serif typeface similar to Tinos.

Desktop:

52–60px
weight 500–600
line-height: 1.05–1.12
max-width: approximately 480px
approximately 2 lines
deep burgundy

Do not make the headline excessively large.

The photograph must remain visually dominant.

Supporting text

“Giáo viên đồng hành, con chủ động khám phá.”

Use Hind Siliguri.

18px
weight 400–500
line-height: 1.45
max-width: approximately 330px
dark neutral color

Do not add additional explanation.

Do not add:

statistics
badges
ratings
“since 20xx”
USP blocks
long paragraphs
promotional claims
10. CTA

CTA text:

“Tìm lớp cho bé →”

Use Hind Siliguri:

15–16px
weight 600
white text

Button:

height: 48–52px
width: approximately 150–165px
horizontal padding: 22–26px
border radius: 8–10px
burgundy or refined pink accent
no excessive shadow

Do not make it a fully rounded pill.

The button should feel premium and controlled.

11. TEXT POSITIONING

Position the entire text block on the LEFT side.

Desktop:

approximately 7–9% from the left edge
vertically slightly below the center of the Hero
left aligned

Structure:

Headline

↓ approximately 20–24px

Supporting text

↓ approximately 28–32px

CTA

Keep the text comfortably inside the photographic negative space.

Do not allow the text to overlap the teacher or child.

Do not center the typography.

The composition should establish:

LEFT = message
RIGHT = human evidence

12. HERO ANIMATION

Keep animation minimal, slow and refined.

Background image

On initial load:

opacity: 0 → 1
scale: 1.03 → 1
duration: 800–1200ms
ease-out

The image should settle completely.

Do not continuously zoom the image.

Headline

Appear approximately 150–200ms after image begins.

opacity: 0 → 1
translateY: 20px → 0
duration: 600–700ms
Supporting text

Appear approximately 150ms after headline.

opacity: 0 → 1
translateY: 12px → 0
duration: approximately 500ms
CTA

Appear approximately 150ms after supporting text.

opacity: 0 → 1
translateY: 12px → 0
duration: approximately 500ms

The complete entrance sequence should settle within approximately 1 second.

CTA hover

Use only:

translateY(-2px)
subtle background-color transition
approximately 200ms
Optional scroll cue

At the bottom of the Hero, a very small downward arrow may be used.

Animation:

translateY 0 → 5px → 0
2–2.5 second loop

Keep it extremely subtle.

13. MOBILE BEHAVIOR

Preserve the same visual concept on mobile.

Header:

Logo + hamburger menu

Do not attempt to fit desktop navigation into mobile.

Mobile menu:

Lớp học
Môi trường
Về chúng tôi
[ Tìm lớp cho bé → ]

Menu entrance:

opacity 0 → 1
translateY(-8px → 0)
approximately 300ms
menu items staggered by approximately 50ms

The Hero image must be cropped intelligently so the teacher and child remain visible.

Preserve the human interaction as the primary visual.

Typography should scale down naturally rather than simply shrinking everything proportionally.

14. PHOTOGRAPHIC REALISM — CRITICAL

The photograph must look genuinely real.

Prioritize:

realistic skin texture
realistic hands and fingers
natural hair
subtle facial expressions
imperfect natural posture
realistic shadows
natural exposure
believable depth of field
subtle photographic grain
realistic classroom imperfections
authentic children's artwork

The image should feel like:

“A professional photographer happened to capture this real moment inside the center.”

Not:

“An AI was asked to create a beautiful education advertisement.”

15. STRICT NEGATIVE DIRECTION

Avoid all of the following:

AI-looking faces
plastic skin
overly smooth skin
distorted hands
perfect fingers
perfect symmetry
exaggerated smiles
children looking at camera
teacher posing for camera
staged interaction
stock-photo aesthetic
generic school photography
kindergarten aesthetic
colorful cartoon decoration
rainbow colors
wooden desks
wood grain
rustic furniture
colorful plastic furniture
cheap classroom appearance
luxury showroom appearance
cinematic lighting
dramatic rim lighting
artificial glow
HDR
excessive sharpening
excessive bokeh
surreal depth of field
perfectly clean classroom
perfectly arranged objects
professionally illustrated children's drawings
digitally perfect artwork
excessive UI decoration
floating doodles
parallax
text-by-character animation
excessive motion
large white text cards
giant CTA
unnecessary badges
unnecessary statistics
unnecessary copy
text inside the photograph
logo generated inside the photograph
16. FINAL EXPERIENCE

The final Hero should make a parent intuitively feel:

“Đây là một môi trường mà con mình có thể thực sự học, tham gia và khám phá.”

The intended visual sequence is:

See the real environment → notice teacher-child interaction → imagine their own child there → read the short message → feel curious → scroll.

Do not explain everything in the Hero.

The photograph creates the experience.
The typography gives it meaning.
The CTA creates the next step.

Keep the final result premium, authentic, spacious, calm, human, and visually confident.

- lower-left area

- approximately y: 64%

- spacing

Approximate visual flow:

                 ENGLISH

                       ↙

              PRE-PRIMARY

==================================================

The shadow should communicate:
"photograph resting on a white surface."

Very soft.
Very low contrast.

- dramatic drop shadows
- glowing shadows
- floating card shadows
- colored shadows

translate(-35px, 20px)

rotate(-6°)

rotate(+5°)

rotate(-3°)

PRE-PRIMARY:
rotate(+6°)

- 700–900ms
- stagger 80–140ms
- natural smooth easing
- very slight physical settling

"four photographs gently landing on a desk."

Do NOT use:
- spinning
- dramatic zoom
- bouncing
- floating
- continuous rotation
- aggressive parallax

After entering:
photographs remain essentially still.

==================================================

TABLET:

MOBILE:

Keep each photograph square.

Maintain generous white space.

- Polaroid frames

PURE WHITE SPACE
+
SMALL HANDMADE DOODLES
+
FOUR REAL SQUARE PHOTOGRAPHS
+
FOUR DIFFERENT LEARNING BEHAVIORS
+
SLIGHT ROTATION
+
ASYMMETRICAL PHYSICAL PLACEMENT
+
SUBTLE "PHOTO ON DESK" ANIMATION.

Design a tall, editorial-style landing page section for an educational center.

1. Overall composition

Create one continuous, very tall section on a pure white background, designed to feel like photographs are physically placed on a clean white tabletop.

The section should have a strong sense of vertical rhythm, whitespace, asymmetry and natural physical placement.

Do not use a standard grid, card layout, equal columns, or a symmetrical gallery.

The visual sequence is strictly:

HÌNH 1 → bên phải
HÌNH 2 → bên trái
HÌNH 3 → bên phải
HÌNH 4 → bên trái

The four photographs are distributed vertically with generous whitespace between them, making the section considerably taller than a normal content section.

2. Heading area

At the beginning of the section, place:

Headline:
“Chọn lớp học phù hợp với con”

Supporting text:
“Mỗi độ tuổi và nhu cầu đều có một cách học phù hợp.”

Keep the typography clean and understated. The heading should introduce the section without competing with the photographs.

3. Photograph composition

Use 4 separate real-life documentary photographs, each in a perfect 1:1 square format.

Each photograph should be slightly larger than before, approximately 380–420px × 380–420px on desktop.

The photographs should feel like actual printed photographs casually placed on a white tabletop.

Absolutely preserve the square shape.

No perspective distortion
No skew
No trapezoid shape
No stretched photographs
No decorative frames
No borders

Each image should have a very subtle soft natural shadow, just enough to create the impression that the photograph physically sits above the white surface.

4. Exact image positioning

IMAGE 1 — Art

Place the first photograph slightly to the right of the central vertical axis.

Rotation: approximately -5°.

Show a Vietnamese child around 7–10 years old independently creating an artwork. The child should be actively drawing/painting/making something rather than posing for the camera.

A teacher may appear subtly in the background, but the teacher should not hold the child's hand or directly control the activity.

Core behavior: CHILD CREATES.

IMAGE 2 — Tutoring

Place the second photograph slightly to the left of the central vertical axis.

Rotation: approximately +4°.

Show a realistic one-to-one tutoring interaction between a Vietnamese student and tutor.

The student should be actively asking, pointing, explaining or discussing something while the tutor responds naturally.

Avoid the typical “student simply looking at textbook while tutor teaches” stock-photo composition.

Core behavior: STUDENT ↔ TUTOR EXCHANGE.

IMAGE 3 — Pre-primary / Handwriting

Place the third photograph slightly to the right of the central vertical axis.

Rotation: approximately +6°.

Show a Vietnamese child around 5–6 years old independently practicing handwriting or a basic learning activity.

The child should look focused and comfortable, not pressured.

A teacher can exist subtly in the background, but the primary visual action must remain with the child.

Core behavior: CHILD PRACTICES.

IMAGE 4 — English Communication

Place the fourth photograph slightly to the left of the central vertical axis.

Rotation: approximately -4°.

Show a Vietnamese child actively communicating with a foreign teacher.

Both sides should participate naturally through eye contact, gestures and conversation.

Avoid a textbook-centered classroom scene.

The image should communicate actual interaction rather than simply “English class.”

Core behavior: CHILD COMMUNICATES.

5. Vertical rhythm

Do not place the four photographs close together.

Create generous vertical whitespace:

Heading

↓

IMAGE 1 — right

↓ large white space

IMAGE 2 — left

↓ large white space

IMAGE 3 — right

↓ large white space

IMAGE 4 — left

The section should feel long and breathable, with each photograph receiving its own visual moment.

Do not let the four images visually merge into one gallery.

6. Natural asymmetry

Although the overall rhythm is:

RIGHT → LEFT → RIGHT → LEFT

do not make the four positions mathematically identical.

Slightly vary:

horizontal offset
rotation angle
vertical spacing
perceived scale

This should feel like someone physically placed four photographs on a table by hand.

Avoid a repetitive “template” feeling.

7. Background decoration

The background remains predominantly pure white.

Add sparse, handmade decorative marks throughout the empty space:

tiny irregular organic shapes
small imperfect circles
tiny loops
small outlined stars / four-point sparkles
dots
subtle paint strokes
miniature color swatches
abstract paper-like shapes
tiny geometric fragments
short pencil marks
small curved marks
tiny playful bursts

These decorations should be independent elements distributed naturally across the section, not attached to specific photographs.

Use very subtle:

graphite gray
dusty pink
muted burgundy
warm gray

Keep visual intensity around 20–35%.

Preserve approximately 85–90% pure white negative space.

The decorations should support the educational/artistic character without becoming a pattern.

8. Photography style

Photography must feel:

documentary
candid
authentic
warm
naturally lit
editorial
realistic Vietnamese educational environment
genuine child–teacher interaction

Avoid:

generic stock photography
overly polished advertising photography
exaggerated smiles
children looking directly at the camera
artificial poses
AI-looking faces
overly cinematic lighting
corporate school imagery

The photographs should look like real moments captured during an actual class.

9. Overall visual direction

The section should communicate:

Different children → different needs → different ways of learning.

The viewer should gradually discover four different learning experiences while scrolling vertically.

The composition should feel playful but controlled, handmade but refined, youthful but not childish.

The dominant visual hierarchy is:

Photographs → whitespace → heading → subtle decorative details

Do not turn the section into a conventional four-card service section.

10. Animation behavior

Each photograph should enter the viewport independently as the user scrolls.

Animation:

subtle fade-in
slight upward movement
small physical settling movement
approximately 700–900ms
natural easing

The photograph should feel as if it is gently settling onto the tabletop.

Do not use:

spinning
bouncing
exaggerated parallax
continuous floating
large zoom
flashy transitions

The rotation of each photograph must remain fixed after entering.

11. Responsive behavior

On mobile, preserve the same fundamental rhythm:

RIGHT → LEFT → RIGHT → LEFT

but reduce the horizontal offsets and photograph size appropriately.

Keep large vertical whitespace between photographs.

Never collapse the section into a 2×2 grid or standard stacked cards.

Final composition principle:

Trong `update()`:
1. Tính `progress` từ 0 → số image - 1 như logic hiện tại.
2. Với mỗi layer:
   - Nếu `i < progress`:

     image phải giữ nguyên:
     `transform: translateY(0)`
     `visibility: visible`

- `translateX`
- `scale`
- offset theo `distance`
- stagger giữa các image phía sau
- transform trên background layers.

layers.forEach(function (el, i) {
  var distance = i - progress;

  if (distance < 0) {
    var amount = Math.min(1, -distance);
    var eased = Math.pow(amount, 1.35);

    el.style.transform =
      'translateY(' + (eased * 115).toFixed(2) + '%)';

    el.style.visibility =
      amount >= 1 ? 'hidden' : 'visible';

  } else {
    el.style.transform = 'translateY(0)';
    el.style.visibility = 'visible';
  }
});
